terms_check: Verbatim check of the quoted sentences against the live pages (weather.gov/disclaimer; waterservices.usgs.gov; the USGS degradation blog; usgs.gov copyrights and crediting pages; api.waterdata.usgs.gov docs footer; IEM disclaimer and home-page footer; water.noaa.gov/about/api; copyright.gov title 17 chapter 1; NWPS swagger info; NWPS home page). Every quoted sentence matches, except that the USGS banner's first sentence lacks the period the record adds. Paraphrases are right in substance but omit: the NWS allowance for unaltered content and name use; the USGS carve-out for non-public-domain site content; and the terms array named in the summary is not in the record file. NOAA-level pages still return 403, so the NOAA statement stays unverified. IEM's conflict stands (public-domain disclaimer; 'All rights reserved' footer on both pages).
recommendation_note: Stands with conditions. The decision holds: IN for a narrow v1 line (NWS flood categories plus USGS annual peak stage per water year, for the nearest flood-stage gauge within 10 miles, from api.waterdata and NWPS), and OUT for daily flood-day counts and 15-minute histories (no daily gage-height series exists for Montana flood-stage gauges, and the 15-minute record only supports a count derived from 15-minute values). The live data reproduce the counts that matter: 277 Montana gauges, 102 with flood stage, 57 with all four categories, 99 flood-stage gauges with a USGS number, the 17.3 percent 10-mile coverage, 12 of 14 towns, the Billings peak and the 2022 flood-day count. The USGS replacement API returns the same values, and the decommission timeline is confirmed. It should not ship as written. Before a build: (1) key the v1 table by USGS number (97 series, 7,084 rows; CBMM8 and CLRM8 duplicate 06185110); (2) make the official-warning polygon test cover every LAT...LON block (Livingston is inside two June 2022 NEW polygons, so the record's '11 towns inside none' is refuted); (3) correct the stated numbers: 42.5 hours, the 72-year median, the 30-75 minute step gaps, the 5-20 point range, the Billings 'three sources', and the annual-peak URL without its parameter filter; (4) add the NWS allowance and the USGS carve-out to the legal basis and keep the per-address gate. None of these changes the IN/OUT call or the 10-mile scope.
